title: Youth Conversation | Tejasvi Surya and K Annamalai
description: Two youth leaders Bengaluru South MP Tejasvi Surya and former IPS officer K Annamalai engage in a lively discussion on youth in politics.  Tune in!

asr.full_text: I'm an IPS officer and Vice President of BJP Tamil Nadu, Shri Anna Malaiji. Heartily welcome to you, to Bangalore and to our office. I request our MP and Dr. Sandeep, BJYM Karnataka President, to please felicitate Shri Anna Malaiji. Thank you, sir. Thank you, sir. Heartly welcome to our member of parliament. And Bharatiya Janata Yuvamurcha president,. Shri Tejasvi Suryaji also. So I'm gifting you a piece,. A turmeric that is grown in a farm in Tamil Nadu. By a farmer called Saravanan in Sethu Malai. Right. Right. Nature is organic one. So, a gift from Tamil Nadu. And this is our Bharathiya, wonderful Bharathiya. So, in his new role, he needs Bharathiya. So, I just want to. This is our Bharathiya, wonderful Bharathiya. So in his new role, he needs Bharathiya. The trend in politics is changing lately. From Ladakh to Kanyakumari, youth are getting into politics and BJP is leading this transformation of politics. In this regard, today we have with us Sri Anna Malaiji and Tejasvi Suryaji. For a very fun-filled discussion which will involve politics, nationalism, different questions. We also have a good gathering here in our office today and we have multiple questions which are posed online also. So we'll just take it forward from there. To start with, Annamalaiji, a question for you. You were a cop, you were in the system, you were in the government. Being in the system, you quit the service, you come to politics. And I'm pretty sure you see a significant role that needs to be played by youth in politics today. You know, how do you see the youth engagement in politics today across the country? What are your views regarding that? It's a very simple data that we have. The median age of the Indian population is very low,. Probably about upwards of 32, 33, 34. And Tejasvi Suryaji, our MP himself, is a very prime example. When leaders of that age come and connect with the bulk of the voters,. Bulk of the voters are below 40. So you represent their aspirations directly without any hindrance. So that is the first positive thing I see. When you compare with other political parties, BJP as a party, it is one step ahead of how the country is changing. It is always one step ahead. It finds youth of great potential, gives them positions, accelerates them, and makes sure that other youths, they revolve around them. That's how the party has grown, right from 1950 till now, in its different avatars. And I believe India itself is becoming an aspirational country. It's becoming an aspirational country. No more people wanted to take things lying down. Everybody is aspirational. And when youth represent that aspirational class,. Come and sit in positions of power,. I see your youth adhyaksha here,. I see all the youth people here,. I see all people not connected to politics,. But still 20-30 of them sitting in this MP's office,. Which is a role model office, I believe. There is a group of youth sitting there,. Running projects on behalf of the MP. Another group of youth doing internship here. This is unlike an MP office, it's more like a corporate office. But here, only because they got connected to a youth,. And maybe they are not associated with the political party. But they are still getting the things done. That's the larger canvas in which I see things. Youth and politics in India. That's a very interesting. Answer on you know how. Youth when they come into politics. Other young people in the country. Will connect I guess we have the next. Question from one of. Our people who are sitting in the audience. In any case i'll just carry forward probably we'll take that question so this is a question. To you also being in mainstream politics and electoral politics youth getting into politics. Is a very good thing we all agree but there is a very significant question which is posed online. Also by multiple people getting into politics in their 20s early 30s is a very challenging thing. For people who come from middle class or lower class of the society. People who come from the rich class, you know,. They don't have to worry about anything else. They can do social work. They can be on the field, get into politics. But for a guy who's in a middle class family. Or a lower middle class family or a poor background,. It's always a question for him on whether to come into politics. And work here or, you know, earn the bread for house. How do you see that a youth who's from a middle class. Or a lower middle class family, in today's scenario,. Getting into politics in his late 20s or early 30s? What is your take on this? I would like to welcome Mr. Anna Malai, who has worked hard to become a BJP member, to. Tamil Nadu. I am very happy to welcome him to our Kachcheri area. I am very happy to welcome him to our Kachcheri area. I am very happy to welcome you to our country. People are seeing this conversation as a national event. Because Anna Malai is not only from Karnataka, but also from other parts of Tamil Nadu. Many young people are following her. So we decided to conduct this conversation in English. So we will continue our conversation in English. We are happy that Annamalai was a DCP in South Bengaluru. That is a very happy thing for us. That is why we are very proud. Another thing is that he had a Hindi posting in Chikmagalur, our place. So we have a relationship there. That is why we are very happy. Sumukh, you've pointed a very important question. There's no easy answer to this. Politics, unfortunately in the last so many years,. Has become a rich man's game. And because it's become a rich man's game,. It is also being infected only by dynasty politics. And this is a vice versa cycle. Politics is rich, politics is expensive, and you have to spend money. Which is why only those people who can spend that kind of money can get into politics. And who are those young people who can spend that kind of money? Those kind of people who inherit that kind of money. And who are the people who can inherit that kind of money? The ones whose father or grandfather has made money through politics, they are the ones who can come into politics. This is the sad state of affairs in India's politics today. So forget contesting elections. A person coming from a middle class family,. I wouldn't even go to the lower middle class or poor background people,. Own people. Even coming from. Families where parents. Are in service jobs, people are in. Monthly. Salaried jobs, their. Children cannot even dream of becoming. MLAs, MPs. My. Story is an exception. But. We need more of these exceptions. To become the norm. And we. Need more and more stories of Narendra. Modi who comes from the. Most poor families. And who shows that they can rise to the highest. Of offices, that should become the norm. And today I do not see any other political party other than the Bharatiya Janata Party. Effectively pushing for reforms, whether it is electoral reforms, whether it is intra-party. Democracy, whether it is encouraging young people in politics, no other party is encouraging. These things. So what happens is, the ones who are Kare Kartas will remain Kare Kartas all their life. The ones who are children of political leaders, they become leaders overnight. Because you have Bab Ka Paisa to invest in politics. So until and unless we break this chain and encourage young people to take up mainstream. Electoral politics, and that is not an easy job, we need electoral reforms which will. Make elections less expensive and more affordable to people. Unless those systemic changes happen, this will not go a long way. This is not just in politics. I was talking to a friend of mine who is working in the movie industry, an aspiring actor. The same thing happens even in Bollywood, happens in other media industries. We have been witnessing after Sushant Singh Rajput's death, we were hearing debates of nepotism. What is nepotism? You may be a great actor, you may be extremely talented. You will keep on giving hundreds of auditions every day. And keep getting rejected. Whereas another person whose father is an actor. He will say, hey you can take my daughter or take my son in your movie. Cast him in your movie. I will give 10% stake or 15% stake and I will also produce the movie. That is why those people who do not have this kind of money. Will not get opportunities to become great actors. So if you look at Bollywood, if you look at Telugu movie industry, any movie industry,. You will find generations of actors' families. Grandfather was actor, father was actor, now the child is also actor. And the grandchildren are also becoming child artists. Does that mean that there are no other capable people, talented people. Who can emote well, act well in those industries? Of course there are. But they don't get an opportunity. The same way, are there no capable leaders? Is there no better young leader than Tejasvi Yadav in whole of Bihar? Are there no young political leaders than MK Stalin in Tamil Nadu? Of course there are hundreds and hundreds of capable young people but they do not get platforms and opportunities. One Anna Malai has come today in Tamil Nadu who will take Tamil Nadu by storm and show what people like MK Stalin in their place. That is the kind of change that we need. So all of us, my commitment as the national president of the URMURJA is to bring more and more young people coming from the most modest of backgrounds, most humblest of families and make them the strongest of leaders for the country. And together as young people, as educated young people of the country, we must push for electoral reforms that our Prime Minister is speaking about. Whether it is one nation, one election. Whether it is one nation, one electoral rolls. Whether it is state funding of elections, electoral bonds. All of these are systemic reforms aimed at making elections more transparent and less expensive, which will bring more young people into the country. So this is what we should all do. It's a big task. But if we can't do it, nobody else will do. Well, that's a very interesting topic that you have opened up. You know, reducing the cost of elections and increasing the youth participation. I think an agenda or a topic can be started just on this. And, you know, if the discussion goes forward, it's going to bring a fundamental change in the way politics happens in this country. I think we have one more question from one of our audience. Very good evening Tejasvi sir and Annamalai sir. So my question is open for both of you. It's like for the women in politics. What are you both going to do for that. Or what are you going to do in the future and now. It's a fact that the women of India are voting for Narendra Modi ji. In large numbers over the last 2-3 years if you see. Women are shifting towards Narendra Modi ji. From there I will answer your question. The reason is, two reasons main. One is,. Politics was always an insecure field for women,. Frankly speaking. Especially if you come to Tamil Nadu,. Dravidian politics, you see,. They never felt safe. Only after Jayalalitha became very powerful,. Women started congregating towards the ADMK. Now Jayalalitha is no more. The reason if you ask me,. Why is this happening? Politics being masculine,. It being powerful, it being. Money oriented business like what he exactly. Portrayed. Any woman. Who was shining in politics either should have had a great. Family background or some powerful. Guy backing her. That's how it was. Now what has happened? The way India is progressing now. Maybe from 1990, accelerated. After Modi Ji's and power two times now. One woman are coming. Out in large numbers especially to BJP. Now we just finished our Veli Yatra in Tamil Nadu. We are very surprised actually. The president and me and couple of people who are travelling with him. Throughout the state, half the crowd. Is women. Among the half. The crowd, women crowd, we felt. Close to 40% of women crowd. Are not connected to the party. They are not party workers. First time they are coming and seeing what. Is a Velayatra, what is BJP doing. When we spoke to a couple of people, they. Said, look there is always a. Pent up emotion inside to get into politics. But till now I never felt safe coming out. For the first time, I am coming out. To see what BJP is doing in. This is a common occurrence across Tamil Nadu. Now the main thing for people like Tejasvi Suryaji and other people who occupy high post in BJP is to make sure, which he has already said,. Is to bring positions of power where women can sit, which BJP is of course doing it. If you see this as a party, for example the national president of BJP women's wing is a lady from our state. If I can take Varnathi Srinivasan as an example and answer, she was just like most of the women in insecure,. Came through AVBP, contested elections. But parties always have got a knack of finding good women. They always make them sit in good posts. One, you have to trust the party. The second point I'm trying to convey is,. Yes, women are coming out in large numbers. They trust BJP. It's an open process. Nobody will scuttle you. Nobody will say there's no demigod above you. And you will not please anybody,. Like being in a movie industry. Now, the second thing,. You've got to trust the party to take care of you. Just like women,. They are trusting the party with their votes. Now, this is the time you've got to trust the party. You need to stick for a little bit more longer time. You need not wait for one year. I've come, nothing I'm getting, can I leave the party now? Just be patient for some more. Time. Big roles are opening up. In fact, if you look at CCS itself,. Nirmala Sitharaman madam is a classic example. From Tamil Nadu, from Andhra,. MP, Rajasabha MP from Karnataka. So now people have. To be a little bit patient. Party. Will reward you. Roles are opening. Up. Democracy itself is getting. More mature. And. Last but not the least,. Narendra Modi ji is emerging as the single largest band leader across India, where women. For the first time are reposing their trust on a national leader. It hasn't happened before anywhere, from Bihar to Telangana to Tamil Nadu. Thank you. Jyotsi, your views on this topic? Very quickly, because you summarized everything so effectively. I think there has to be an active interest taken at every level. In fact after I became the national president of the Yuva Morcha, I reminded all Yuva Morcha. Cadres across the country that this party, the Bharti Janata party among its founding. Members had Vijay Mate, Vijay Rajay, Sindhya as its founding member and she was such a. Two, whether it is economics, politics, social, like the Constitution of India says, we must. Strive towards creating equality of opportunities. So opportunity needs to be created to people. As strong leaders both inside and outside of the party. And it's a great, great sign of the modern and changing times that even in Bihar elections,. Which Mr. Malai ji very rightly mentioned, the polling percentage of women is 10% more. Than the polling percentage of men in the country. And if you look at how women vote, women are far more sensitive voters, far more responsible. Voters and far more long term thinking voters than menfolk, which is why the Prime Minister. Was rewarded for his works. And let me also tell you, my visits in Bengal, I am seeing a large number of women coming. Out on the streets. On earth can stop the change from happening. Even in West Bengal, which is the land of. The Shakti, the women folk of West Bengal are actually leading the fight for the BJP.
